questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These tractors are hard to operate and require careful driving.

questions.question: To check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Check for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to:
questions.explanation: In vehicles with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: More than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by:
questions.explanation: More than half of truck driver deaths from accidents happen because of truck rollovers. To prevent rollovers, keep cargo low and centered on your rig. Turn corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Looking ahead at the road:

options.text: Is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors
Does not help you drive more safely
Helps you avoid sudden lane changes

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you avoid sudden lane changes
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous when driving a combination vehicle. Looking ahead allows you to see obstacles coming and plan lane changes early, so you don't have to make sudden moves.

questions.question: When braking with a trailer that has anti-lock brakes, you should:

options.text: Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with anti-lock brakes, brake the same way you would if the vehicle did not have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, the seals should be pressed together at a ____ angle.
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, couple the correct ones and press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise landing gear completely before driving. If it is not fully raised, it can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: Shut-off valves:

options.text: Stop air from leaving air brake systems
Stop air from entering air brake systems
Take control of vehicles that are out of control

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving air brake systems
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. Always keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, you should:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Leave one pair of glad hands loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They may be color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ­­­­­____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require more driving skill to operate than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over than empty rigs. The heavy cargo raises the center of gravity, making rollover more likely.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle:

options.text: Will not make a difference in braking.
Will give you better control when braking.
Will likely cause the air brakes to fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will give you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even with anti-lock brakes on just one axle, you will have more control while braking than you would have without anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away from the trailer's air braking system:

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, there will be no brakes on the trailer and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving because:

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line supplies air to the trailer air tanks. It also controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color identifies service lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes when coupling. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: The tractor protection valve:

options.text: Ensures the engine gets proper oil lubrication.
Protects the tractor from exceeding a set speed.
Keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. It closes automatically if pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Rearward amplification refers to:

options.text: The amount of noise at the rear of the vehicle.
The number of trailers one tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the "crack-the-whip" effect. If not handled properly, this effect can cause a trailer to tip over.
